stories.title: A Phius-certified passive house in Massachusetts
stories.summary: Fine Homebuilding named this Massachusetts residence its 2026 New House of the Year. Designed by ZeroEnergy Design, the home features Scandinavian modern aesthetics, sustainable materials, and an 18-meter basement archery range. The project prioritizes energy efficiency and aging in place. It is a house with a target.

stories.title: Neral railway station receives IGBC gold rating
stories.summary: Neral station on the Central Railway has been awarded a gold rating by the Indian Green Building Council. The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation spent over Rs 80 crore on upgrades, including a 375 kWp rooftop solar system. The station now features energy-efficient lighting and fans.

stories.title: Central Railway
stories.summary: Mumbai: Neral railway station on Central Railway has received a Gold rating from the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC), recognising its efforts to combine environmentally sustainable infrastructure with improved passenger facilities. The rating follows the final assessment conducted this month and marks a significant milestone in the Mumbai Railway Vikas

stories.title: Pickering community centre earns zero carbon certification
stories.summary: The City of Pickering has received a Zero Carbon Building certification for its new Dorsay Community and Heritage Centre. The facility uses mass timber, low-carbon concrete, and air-to-water heat pumps. Officials state these design choices support biodiversity and reduce both operational and embodied carbon.

Karnataka proposes 10 tree parks for Bengaluru
stories.summary: The Karnataka government has proposed a Rs 150-crore project to develop 10 tree parks and arboretums across 3,271 acres in and around Bengaluru. The initiative aims to restore green cover, conserve biodiversity, and combat urban heat caused by rapid urbanisation.

stories.title: Temple architecture attracts new students
stories.summary: Traditional Indian temple design is seeing a surge in interest, with over 200 students now pursuing specialised studies in the field. Architect D.N.V. Prasad Sthapathy noted that the rise in temple construction across the country is creating new opportunities for trained sculptors and artisans.

stories.title: Maciej Nowicki’s Chandigarh Planning Ideas Revisited
stories.summary: A documentary screened during the International Film Festival of India in Goa is bringing renewed attention to Polish-American architect Maciej Nowicki, whose early ideas influenced parts of Chandigarh’s original urban vision. Titled Nirmanjali: The Chandigarh of Maciej Nowicki, the non-feature documentary by National Award-winning filmmaker Suraj Kumar examines Nowicki’s contribution

stories.title: CEPT University to host winter exhibition
stories.summary: CEPT University will host its Winter Exhibition 2026 from November 24 to December 4 in Ahmedabad. The 11-day event will display the work of 1,838 students across 115 studio units, featuring models, prototypes, and design concepts developed over the past four months.

stories.title: New Delhi to host India Biennale 2026
stories.summary: New Delhi will host the second India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale from December 4, 2026, to March 21, 2027. The 108-day event will use a city-wide format across museums, galleries, and public spaces, following its inaugural edition at the Red Fort.

stories.title: Stepped-roof university wins architecture prize
stories.summary: Prestige University in India has been named World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival. The project features a stepped roof that doubles as an open-air auditorium. The design is intended to evoke ancient Indian stepwells, though it also bears a resemblance to Escher drawings.

stories.title: Sanjay Puri Architects wins top festival honor
stories.summary: Sanjay Puri Architects received the World Building of the Year award for Prestige University in Indore, India. The campus building includes 463 stepped platforms designed to function as a public event space for up to 9,000 students. The festival concluded this week in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

stories.title: Brussels opens massive former factory museum
stories.summary: Kanal opens in Brussels on 28 November as a cultural centre housed in a former 40,000 square metre Citroën factory. Following a decade of development, the project is being marketed as Europe's largest museum development. It is now larger than London's Tate Modern.

stories.title: ZHA completes first African theatre in Rabat
stories.summary: The Théâtre Royal de Rabat has opened on the banks of the Bouregreg River, marking ZHA's first completed project in Africa. Sixteen years after the initial design presentation, the building now houses three performance venues and a restaurant within a single white volume following the river's topography.

stories.title: Doha terminal designed for dual-purpose use
stories.summary: The Grand Terminal in Doha has opened as a cruise facility and festival venue. Architect Ashley Munday stated the project is designed to absorb uses like markets and exhibitions throughout the year. The terminal is currently serving as a festival site for the World Cup.

stories.title: Team De Mussen wins Utrecht block tender
stories.summary: A consortium including Orange Architects and SO to IL has won the tender for urban block 1B in Utrecht. The project, titled De Mussen, aims to integrate 166 homes with education and childcare facilities. This marks the first major architectural work in the Netherlands for the New York-based firm SO

stories.title: Ecuador music venue design unveiled
stories.summary: Architects have completed the design for Bombódromo, a performing arts campus in Ecuador's Chota Valley. Commissioned by the local prefecture, the project aims to blend indoor and outdoor spaces for cultural events. The architects hope the venue will eventually be built for public use.

stories.title: London Museum opens in historic market
stories.summary: The London Museum opens its new home in the Smithfield General Market on 28 November. The project, led by Stanton Williams and Asif Khan Studio, involved a decade of adaptive reuse to convert the Victorian trade centre. It aims to connect the city's heritage with its urban identity.

stories.title: Meta secures priority access to low-carbon cement
stories.summary: Sublime Systems has signed an agreement to provide Meta with priority access to its low-carbon cement for data centre construction. While cement is rarely sold on multi-year, fixed-volume terms, the deal aims to help the company address supply chain emissions as it builds out AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Mass timber market projected to grow
stories.summary: The global mass timber construction market is forecast to reach $1.3 billion by 2030, according to industry data. RedBuilt is promoting hybrid timber systems, citing faster installation times and lower carbon footprints. The broader timber construction industry is expected to reach $44.2 billion by 2035.

stories.title: ICON begins largest 3D printed commercial building
stories.summary: Construction firm ICON has started printing a 12,649-square-foot facility in San Antonio. The building uses a mixed structural system, combining 3D printed walls with a 60-ton steel superstructure to accommodate heavy machinery. Completion is expected in summer 2027.

stories.title: Researchers print lunar bricks from dust
stories.summary: A University of Arkansas team has demonstrated a method to fuse lunar regolith into stackable building blocks using a low-power light source. The researchers claim the bricks require no binding agent. The process aims to reduce the weight of cargo sent from Earth for future lunar settlements.

stories.title: 3D concrete printing market growth forecast
stories.summary: The global 3D concrete printing market is projected to reach $36.65 billion by 2033, growing at a compound annual rate of 61.82 percent. The industry is adopting automated methods to reduce labour dependency and accelerate construction. Asia Pacific currently holds a 55.54 percent market share.

Recycled PU board market growth expected
stories.summary: The global recycled polyurethane boards market is projected to reach $10.60 billion by 2033, according to Coherent Market Insights. Growth is attributed to rising demand for sustainable insulation and energy-efficient construction materials. Manufacturers are currently increasing investments in both mechanical and chemical recycling technologies.

stories.title: Recycled steel market growth forecast
stories.summary: The global recycled steel market is projected to reach $478.5 billion by 2035, growing at a compound annual rate of 4.82 percent. The industry is shifting toward sustainable production methods and increased use of ferrous scrap, driven by carbon emission regulations and environmental concerns.

stories.title: Karnataka CM tours Japan to study waste management
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar visited the Maishima incineration plant in Osaka to study waste-to-energy models. The facility processes 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily and generates 32 MW of power. The state aims to adopt these international practices for its own urban infrastructure and environmental management.

stories.title: Karnataka CM studies Osaka waste-to-energy technology
stories.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar visited the Maishima incineration plant in Osaka to observe its waste-to-energy operations. The facility has been operational since 2001, processing 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily to generate 32 MW of electricity. The plant meets its own energy needs and supplies the local grid.

stories.title: Karnataka CM explores Nagoya underground infrastructure
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar visited Nagoya to study the Sakae underground network and public transport models. The state government is exploring global best practices in urban planning and mobility to improve the efficiency and sustainability of its own cities. The visit focused on integrated urban infrastructure systems.

stories.title: Beginners learn quilting at Gee’s Bend festival
stories.summary: The fifth annual Airing of the Quilts Festival in Gee’s Bend, Alabama, hosted a workshop for beginners to stitch 12-by-12-inch quilt squares. Celebrated quilters Doris Pettway Mosely and Mary Margaret Pettway provided instruction and feedback to attendees during the morning session. The event celebrates the community’s long-standing quilting tradition.

stories.title: Preserving the appeal of classic terrazzo floors
stories.summary: Terrazzo floors remain a popular design choice despite decades of reinvention. The material, once common in mid-century interiors, continues to hold a distinct appeal for homeowners. Seven featured residences, including a villa in New Delhi, demonstrate why the original flooring remains a sought-after feature in modern architecture.

stories.title: Photographs document female bodybuilders in Kerala
stories.summary: Artist Keerthana Kunnath is presenting her debut series, Not What You Saw, at Foam in Amsterdam. The exhibition features photographs of female bodybuilders in Kerala, exploring the intersection of physical construction and the way bodies are framed by the camera. The series highlights the community's daily lives.

stories.title: NGT penalizes builder for lack of environmental clearance
stories.summary: The National Green Tribunal has ordered Sandhu Builders to pay environmental compensation equal to 5 percent of the project cost for constructing the Sandhu Palace in Mumbai without clearance. The tribunal also barred the developer from creating third-party interests and restricted the local municipal corporation from issuing occupation certificates.

stories.title: High Court clears Chembur redevelopment project
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court upheld an appellate tribunal decision to set aside a 2025 RERA order that stalled a housing redevelopment project. The court noted that delaying the project further would only increase the hardship for original society members who had already vacated their homes a decade ago.

stories.title: Delhi-Panipat-Karnal corridor approved for 2030
stories.summary: The National Highways Authority of India approved the 136.3-km Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor. The project, managed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation, will cost approximately 33,051 crore rupees. Officials expect the corridor to reduce travel time and expand real estate opportunities in Haryana by its 2030 completion.

stories.title: Gangtok promotes pedestrian-friendly urban planning
stories.summary: Gangtok is utilizing protected footpaths, tactile tiles, and elevated walkways to improve urban mobility. The city’s infrastructure includes a 12-km footpath along its main highway, intended to separate pedestrians from vehicular traffic. The capital of Sikkim is positioning itself as a model for sustainable and accessible city design.

stories.title: Volunteers plant 1,000 trees to mitigate urban flooding
stories.summary: Charlotte Mecklenburg Storm Water Services organized a planting event to install 1,000 tree saplings near Long Creek. The initiative aims to address urban flooding by restoring forest cover along stream banks. Environmental specialist Matthew Peine noted that the trees will require several years to reach full maturity.

stories.title: Miami-Dade County opens electric bus facility
stories.summary: Miami-Dade County has opened the South Dade Transit Operations Center following two years of construction. The new facility provides 100 dedicated spaces for electric buses. The project represents a significant investment in the county's transit infrastructure and fleet electrification efforts.

stories.title: New loan program targets vacant Brooklyn apartments
stories.summary: The Subordinate Market Rate Revolving Term Loan program aims to revitalize vacant buildings in New York City. The initiative seeks to recycle funds from previous city-backed projects to support new housing goals. The program is designed to bring long-vacant properties back into active use.

stories.title: Architecture firms announce new job openings
stories.summary: Five architecture and design firms, including Rapt Studio and Cass Calder Smith, have listed new job openings in New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Connecticut. The roles range from junior designers to project architects, reflecting current hiring activity across several major design hubs.

stories.title: Expert argues cities should regulate surveillance tech
stories.summary: A former police chief suggests that local governments possess the tools to limit the use of automated license plate readers. By controlling municipal funding, cities can prevent surveillance technology from targeting residents. The expert advocates for greater local oversight of police technology procurement and deployment.

stories.title: Rapid urban growth challenges India’s livability
stories.summary: India’s cities are expanding rapidly, bringing new infrastructure and economic opportunities. However, persistent issues with traffic congestion, pollution, and water shortages continue to impact the quality of life. The challenge remains to ensure that urban development prioritizes the everyday needs of residents alongside modernization.

stories.title: Municipal budgets face revenue growth slowdown
stories.summary: The National League of Cities reports that finance officers are increasingly concerned about meeting municipal needs. Declining federal aid, plateauing tax revenues, and rising infrastructure costs are placing significant pressure on city budgets. Many cities are struggling to balance fiscal requirements with the demand for public services.

stories.title: Transport hubs reimagined as public spaces
stories.summary: New architectural projects are transforming train stations and airports into venues for libraries, sports facilities, and community kitchens. These designs aim to move beyond traditional transit functions, treating waiting areas as spaces for public life. The trend suggests a shift in how transport hubs accommodate passengers.

stories.title: Synaps 2.0: Rethinking architectural design with AI
stories.summary: Architecture has long relied on translating abstract intentions into technical documentation, a process that remains time-consuming despite decades of digital tools. Synaps 2.0 aims to address this gap, following the industry shift from manual drawing boards to CAD and Building Information Modeling. Translation remains a persistent architectural task.

stories.title: JobTread software lands on Deloitte Fast 500
stories.summary: Dallas-based JobTread Software ranked sixth on the 2025 Deloitte Technology Fast 500, citing 11,944% growth. The company provides construction-management software for builders and contractors. It leads the North Texas companies on the list, according to Deloitte’s official winner data.

stories.title: Vertiv and Nvidia partner to cut AI data center deployment times, aiming for 30% more token output in year one. - Pluang
Marlowe raises $277 million for AI hardware
stories.summary: Marlowe has raised $277 million to deploy AI on a non-NVIDIA chip foundation, citing a 40% increase in data center construction costs since 2020. The company plans to tweak chips from AMD and Etched to optimize systems for AI inference. Operating AI is becoming more difficult to finance.

stories.title: Aiden AI raises $32 million from A91 Partners
stories.summary: Aiden AI, an enterprise startup founded by former Infosys executive Srinivas Kamadi, has raised $32 million in its first institutional funding round. The company plans to use the capital to help large firms deploy AI across legacy systems, specifically targeting banking and insurance sectors.

stories.title: Supertake raises $20 million for AI investment platform
stories.summary: Supertake has raised $20 million in seed funding to develop a platform that converts user market opinions into portfolios managed by AI agents. The company claims its technology makes professional-style portfolio construction accessible to those lacking time or expertise. The round included participation from Coinbase Ventures.

stories.title: Reversa raises €750,000 for regulatory compliance AI
stories.summary: Spanish legal tech startup Reversa has raised €750,000 in pre-seed funding to expand its AI-powered regulatory compliance platform. The company previously joined A&O Shearman’s tech incubator program earlier in 2026. The funds are earmarked for hiring and further product development.

stories.title: Sylvia Lavin named dean of Princeton School of Architecture
stories.summary: Sylvia Lavin has been appointed dean of the Princeton School of Architecture after serving in the role on an interim basis since January. Lavin, a historian and curator, intends to renew conversations between design, history, theory, and building technology while emphasizing a global perspective.

stories.title: Delhi airport ranks 38th in TIME global list
stories.summary: Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport ranked 38th out of 47 major airports in TIME magazine’s 2027 list. Compiled with Statista, the ranking evaluated passenger experience and operational performance. Singapore’s Changi Airport took the top spot, while IGI remains India's sole representative in the major airports category.

stories.title: UW Architecture student market returns to Galt for the holidays - CambridgeToday.ca
UNSW Built Environment exhibition opens in December
stories.summary: The 2026 UNSW Built Environment graduation exhibition, titled To Be, opens on 4 December at the White Bay Power Station. The three-day event showcases work from seven disciplines, including architecture and construction management, featuring panel discussions and networking opportunities for graduates and industry professionals.

stories.title: Punahou students race 3D-printed cars
stories.summary: Students at Punahou Academy applied engineering and physics principles to design and race 3D-printed Formula One cars powered by CO2 cartridges. The project required students to use CAD software and precision measurements to optimize aerodynamics and performance, combining STEM concepts with model car racing.

stories.title: Banaras Hindu University students explore heritage
stories.summary: Students at Banaras Hindu University are participating in experiential learning activities focused on the temple architecture and spiritual heritage of Varanasi. The program precedes the fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam, which is scheduled to take place from 28 November through 12 December 2026.

stories.title: Liverpool and XJTLU celebrate 20-year partnership
stories.summary: Professor Youmin Xi accepted the Freedom of the City of Liverpool to mark the 20th anniversary of Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University. The institution, a partnership between the University of Liverpool and Xi’an Jiaotong University, has hosted over 17,000 students through its 2+2 pathway since its establishment in 2006.

stories.title: Dieterich school board plans tax rate reduction
stories.summary: The Dieterich Unit 30 school board is aiming for a lower tax rate in 2027, though officials noted that exact figures depend on property valuations arriving next year. The board also hired an architect to manage renovations for the district’s 1939 gymnasium.

stories.title: India and Nepal launch Saryu-Kamla Express
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah inaugurated the Saryu-Kamla Express, a 604-km rail service connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur Dham. The cross-border route is intended to facilitate pilgrimages between the two cities, which are associated with the Ramayana.

research.title: Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming. By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again.

research.title: Earth’s ancient oceans may have fooled scientists about its oxygen history
research.summary: Earth’s journey from an oxygen-starved world to a planet capable of supporting complex life may have unfolded very differently than scientists once believed. A new analysis suggests that oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere in three major stages, with the oceans taking millions or even hundreds of millions of.

research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Across the sciences, researchers have developed hundreds of statistics that describe the collective behavior of complex systems. research.title: Growing Hypergraphs with Homophily
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: There are many extant models of hypergraphs with interactions governed by attribute-based homophily between nodes, but most assume independence between edges conditional on node parameters. Relaxing this assumption, we study a mechanistic model of growing hypergraphs. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
